name: Guitar
origin: Spain; the modern classical design developed in the 19th century.
description: Players pluck or strum the strings. Pressing a string at a fret changes its vibrating length and pitch.

name: Violin
description: The violin has four strings. A bow makes them vibrate, and its wooden body helps the sound resonate.

name: Cello
description: The cello is a large bowed string instrument. A seated player supports it on an endpin.

name: Flute
origin: Ancient flutes occur in many cultures; the modern concert flute developed in Europe.
description: Air blown across an opening creates sound. Keys change the effective length of the air column.

name: Trumpet
origin: Ancient ceremonial horns; modern valved designs developed in 19th-century Europe.
description: Vibrating lips produce sound. Valves change the length of tubing to help select notes.

name: Saxophone
origin: Developed by Adolphe Sax in the 1840s.
description: A single reed vibrates when air passes through the mouthpiece. It is a woodwind instrument despite its metal body.

name: Drum Kit
origin: United States, late 19th and early 20th centuries.
description: A drum kit combines drums and cymbals. Sticks and pedals let one musician create layered rhythms.

name: Tabla
origin: Indian subcontinent; its precise historical development is debated.
description: Tabla are two hand drums. Players use fingers and palms to produce many tones.

name: Xylophone
origin: Historical forms developed in parts of Africa and Asia.
description: Mallets strike tuned wooden bars. Shorter bars generally produce higher notes.

name: Piano
origin: Invented by Bartolomeo Cristofori in Italy around 1700.
description: Pressing a key makes a hammer strike strings. The keyboard is the playing interface; the sound comes from vibrating strings.

name: Accordion
origin: Early modern designs appeared in 19th-century Europe.
description: Bellows move air past reeds. Keys or buttons select the notes.

name: Pipe Organ
origin: Ancient Greece; later developed extensively in Europe.
description: Keys control air flowing through pipes. Stops select groups of pipes with different sounds.
